feature: Pillar pages (#1485/#1621, screen 12) — the six real pillar landing pages in artifacts/portal, wired to the already-built GET /api/portal/pillars (pillar-summary-stats.ts). Real design landed in Design/portal/design_handoff_full_site/screens/Pillar Pages.dc.html; pages live at artifacts/portal/src/pages/pillar.tsx, route /pillars/:pillar, reached from the shell's PillarTabStrip. Scope: pillar summary cards + scores only — the design's full per-check 'block' breakdown and the click-a-finding-for-full-breakdown + SOP/Runbook remediation offer are a real, separate follow-up (#1621's own open architecture questions).
notes: shaneapp://runTest was not reachable from this build session (the mcp shane-msp tool set exposed to this session carries no runTest/executeSql tool this time, and the local dev-server process was also down on port 8080 at build time) — this manifest is written and registered but NOT live-executed this session. Real verification performed instead: `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean, and `vite build` clean, on artifacts/portal.

apiTests prove the real, already-built backend contract directly: log in via POST /api/auth/login, extract a bearer token, then exercise GET /api/portal/pillars exactly as usePillarPage.ts's own fetchWithAuth call does.

PILLAR_SUMMARY_KEYS order is fixed server-side (pillar-summary-stats.ts, asserted by its own cross-app order test) and reused here: governance=0, licensing=1, adoption=2, compliance=3, health=4, security=5, copilot=6 — asserted by index rather than a JSONPath filter (HttpTestExecutor.cs's TryResolveJsonPath has no `[?(@...)]` filter support, #3052).
No write assertions: /api/portal/pillars is a pure read (buildPillarSummary), so there is nothing to round-trip or restore.
ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD — the same CustomerUser testbed account other portal manifests use.

UI steps deliberately assert the honest-state scaffolding (page shell, score hero, findings section) rather than exact score numbers or finding titles, which are real tenant data that changes with every scan run.
